To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
methylation might be a critical regulatory switch in the life cycle of mRNA, and its redox-dependent regulation might play a role in synaptic plasticity, cognition, and behavior.

(1) DNA and mRNA methylation are highly correlated and both are influenced by glutathione anti oxidant levels, (2) glutathione anti oxidation levels are highly correlated to synaptic protein expression levels, and (3) mRNA methylation levels are highly correlated with protein expression.

(1) DNA methylation changes in the brain are highly correlated to learning and memory, (2) RNA methylation changes in brain are recently characterized, (3) DNA methylation and RNA methylation changes can be interrelated, and (4) redox status of the brain might be a central regulatory switch for the methylation-based changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a novel hypothesis that methylated RNA might be the critical regulatory factor for the lifespan, processing, and maturation of mRNA, and thus, the regulation of protein expression, synaptic plasticity, and memory.
understanding the functional implications of methylation in mRNA processing, translation, and protein synthesis.
a redox-based methylation switch, and its influence on pre- and post-transcriptional maturation of mRNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
methylation is a central regulatory switch for the life cycle of mRNA, which might have implications in synaptic function and plasticity, learning, and memory, and thus in neurological disorders.
, redox-based methylation changes in neurons are important for normal cognition, learning, and memory, and alterations in these methylation changes might lead to cognitive and memory deficits.

, the redox-based methylation switch, which is regulated by the glutathione-anti-oxidant system, is an important regulator for the maturation, processing and stability of mRNA, and therefore, protein expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
methylation-based mRNA processing is the central switch for regulating the expression of synaptic and cytoplamic proteins.
methylation might be a redox-based regulatory switch for the mRNA life-cycle and protein turnover in the brain.
the methylation switch might act as a central regulatory switch for mRNA processing, protein synthesis, and turnover, and thus it might influence cognition and memory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the redox-based methylation switch might be an important regulator of the mRNA life cycle and protein turnover.
methylation might be the key regulator of mRNA life-cycle, and that the redox status in neurons is a central regulator of methylation.
the role of methylation in mRNA processing is a critical factor in neuronal function, which needs to be considered in future studies.
